name: Vitamin C and zinc pit routine
lead: The "vitamin C and zinc pit routine" is an informal underarm-care practice discussed in grooming circles as a way to manage body odor, typically involving topical or dietary vitamin C and zinc. It is described as anecdotal, and no published studies of this specific routine were located.
Background on how underarm odor arises is available: bacteria on the skin break down apocrine sweat secretions into odorous compounds, and genetics, diet and health also influence odor.[1]

paras: Body odor is attributed mainly to skin bacteria acting on apocrine sweat in the armpits, with variation linked to genes such as ABCC11.[1] Established approaches described include antibacterial soap, deodorant and antiperspirant.[1]

card.summary: An anecdotal underarm-odor routine built on vitamin C and zinc, with no studies behind it.
card.note: Anecdotal only; persistent odor may warrant a medical check.

quick.overview:
This routine is an informal approach to underarm odor that people describe using vitamin C and zinc.

The practice is anecdotal and no published trials of it were found.
quick.mechanism: Underarm odor is generally attributed to bacteria breaking down sweat. Proponents of the routine have not had their mechanism tested in published research.
quick.risks: No specific harms are documented for the routine itself. Persistent odor is sometimes linked to medical causes.
